title: Forecasting and escalating exceptions
blurb: Use forecasts to spot a likely tolerance breach early and escalate it to the right level, without acting beyond delegated authority.
question: A team manager forecasts that a work package will breach its time tolerance, but the stage will stay within its tolerances. Who handles this, and does the project board need an exception report?

teach.body: Formally, a forecast is a prediction of future performance, made by extrapolating trends, using data or applying judgement. Progress reviews are not only about what has happened: they also estimate the remaining work and where the plan is heading. In plain English: the useful question is not 'are we late today?' but 'will we finish inside our limits?'

teach.h: Forecast cost against the stage tolerance
teach.caption: By week 5 the trend shows the stage will cross tolerance. That forecast is the exception: escalate now, not after the money is spent.

teach.h: Escalating: to the next level, as early as possible
teach.body: An exception is a situation where it can be forecast that a deviation will go beyond the tolerance levels agreed between the project manager and the board, or between the board and the business layer. When a breach is forecast, the level holding the tolerance passes the decision up one level. It does not act beyond its own delegated authority, and it does not wait for the breach to happen.

teach.h: Does the board need an exception report?

children.label: PM handles it in the stage

teach.h: Only stage and project exceptions reach the board
teach.body: Exceptions at work package level are handled by the project manager in controlling a stage, for example by corrective action or rearranging work packages. If the project manager can resolve an issue within stage tolerance, no exception report is needed. Only exceptions to stage or project plans go to the project board.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a regional flood barrier
teach.body: At Severnside Environment Agency, team manager Callum Reid forecasts that piling will finish eight days beyond his work package tolerance. He raises this with project manager Nadia Hussain as an issue. Nadia's stage still has three weeks of time tolerance, so she reorders two work packages and the stage stays inside its limits: no exception report. A month later, steel prices push the stage forecast 12% over a 10% cost tolerance, and Nadia raises an exception report to the board that day.

teach.caption: Each level escalates only what is beyond its own tolerance.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) An exception is a FORECAST breach: waiting for the actual overrun is too late. (2) A team manager escalates to the project manager, never straight to the board. (3) If the issue can be resolved inside stage tolerance, no exception report is raised: escalating within tolerance goes against manage by exception. (4) A breach of project tolerance goes beyond the board to the business layer.

items: A forecast predicts future performance from trends, data and judgement.
Progress reviews look forward as well as back.
Escalate to the next level up as soon as a breach is forecast.
Work package exceptions are handled by the PM; only stage or project exceptions reach the board.
Within stage tolerance: no exception report.

summary: You can now use a forecast to spot a likely breach early and escalate it one level up: team manager to project manager, project manager to board, board to business layer. You know that issues resolvable within stage tolerance need no exception report.

A.q: When should a project manager escalate a stage tolerance problem to the project board?
options: When the stage has already gone over budget
When the next scheduled highlight report is due
When a breach of stage tolerance is forecast
When the team manager raises any issue
A.why: An exception exists as soon as a breach can be forecast, so the project manager escalates then, as early as possible.

whyNot.0: Waiting for an actual overspend is too late; the trigger is the forecast.
whyNot.1: A forecast breach is escalated straight away, not held for the next highlight report.
whyNot.3: Many issues can be resolved within stage tolerance without involving the board.

A.q: A team manager forecasts a breach of work package tolerance. To whom should it be escalated?
options: The project board
The project manager
The senior supplier
The business layer
A.why: Team managers escalate forecast work package breaches to the project manager, as an issue.

whyNot.0: Team managers do not escalate directly to the board.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier sits on the board; the team manager reports to the project manager.
whyNot.3: The business layer deals with forecast breaches of project tolerance.

A.q: What is a forecast in the progress practice?
options: A record of the actual progress to date
A permissible deviation from the target
A summary of stage status for the board
A prediction of future performance
A.why: A forecast is a prediction of future performance, using trends, data and judgement.

whyNot.0: Actual progress to date is what forecasts start from, not the forecast itself.
whyNot.1: A permissible deviation from a target is a tolerance.
whyNot.2: A summary of stage status for the board is a highlight report.

B.q: A work package is forecast to run five days late, but the stage remains within its time tolerance. What should happen?
options: The PM resolves it in the stage without an exception report
The PM raises an exception report to the project board
The team manager escalates it to the project executive
The board asks the business layer for more project time
B.why: Work package exceptions are handled by the project manager in controlling a stage; within stage tolerance, no exception report is needed.

whyNot.1: An exception report is needed only when stage or project tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.
whyNot.2: Team managers escalate to the project manager, not the executive.
whyNot.3: The project tolerance is not threatened, so the business layer is not involved.

B.q:
Which two statements about escalating are correct?
1. Only exceptions to stage or project plans go to the project board.
2. A team manager escalates forecast work package breaches to the board.
3. An exception should be escalated as early as possible.
4. The project manager may exceed stage tolerance if the cause is outside the project.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Only stage or project exceptions reach the board (1), and exceptions are escalated as early as possible (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: team managers escalate to the project manager.
whyNot.2: Both are false: escalation goes to the PM, and the PM cannot act beyond stage tolerance.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: a forecast stage breach must go to the board whatever its cause.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. An exception is a situation where it can be [?] that there will be a deviation beyond agreed tolerance levels.
options: shown
confirmed
measured
forecast
B.why: The definition of an exception rests on a forecast, so escalation can happen before the breach.

whyNot.0: The definition does not require proof; it is based on a prediction.
whyNot.1: Waiting for confirmation would delay escalation.
whyNot.2: Measuring describes actuals; the exception is defined by a forecast.

C.q: The project board forecasts that the project will exceed its cost tolerance. Who decides, and where did that tolerance come from?
options: The executive; the stage plan
The business layer; the project mandate
The project board; the business case
The project manager; the project plan
C.why: The business layer sets project tolerances, often in the mandate, and decides on forecast breaches of project tolerance.

whyNot.0: Project tolerance is set by the business layer, not in a stage plan, and the executive cannot decide beyond it.
whyNot.2: The board cannot decide on a breach of tolerance set by the level above it.
whyNot.3: The project manager works within stage tolerance and cannot decide on project tolerance.

C.q: A project manager forecasts a stage overspend beyond cost tolerance and, without telling the board, drops products from the stage beyond its scope tolerance to stay within budget. What is wrong with this?
options: Scope cuts must be recorded in the lessons log first
The team manager should have raised the exception
The PM is acting beyond delegated authority
Cost tolerances do not apply during a stage
C.why: A forecast breach of stage tolerance must be escalated to the board in an exception report; cutting scope beyond the stage scope tolerance is outside the PM's delegated authority.

whyNot.0: The lessons log records lessons; it is not a gate for scope decisions.
whyNot.1: Stage-level exceptions are raised by the project manager, not the team manager.
whyNot.3: Stage cost tolerances are set by the board and apply throughout the stage.

C.q: Which use of a forecast best supports manage by exception?
options: Showing the board each week's actual costs
Spotting a likely breach early to escalate it
Recording the final costs for the lessons log
Widening the stage tolerance to fit the forecast
C.why: Forecasting lets the level holding a tolerance see a breach coming and alert the next level as early as possible.

whyNot.0: Actual costs show the past; manage by exception relies on forecasts.
whyNot.2: Recording final costs supports learning, not early escalation.
whyNot.3: Stage tolerances are set by the project board; the project manager cannot widen them to absorb a forecast breach.

reteach.title: The rising river
reteach.question: Why does a lock keeper warn the town when the river is forecast to flood, not when water is in the streets?

blocks.body: A lock keeper can handle a small rise by opening sluices. When the forecast shows the river will top the banks tomorrow, that is beyond what she can manage, so she warns the town council today. She does not try to build a new flood wall on her own authority. Project escalation follows the same pattern: act within your limits, and pass a forecast breach up one level, early.

blocks.text: Warning the council about every small rise wastes their time; staying silent until the streets flood is too late. Escalate forecast breaches only, and early.

explain.body: Progress reviews are not confined to looking backwards: they forecast the remaining work and the likely outcome.

test.q: What is the main value of forecasting in progress reviews?
options: It records actual costs for the business case
It sets the tolerance levels for each stage
It shows where the plan is heading in time to act
It replaces checkpoint reports from team managers
test.why: Forecasting shows the likely outcome so deviations can be dealt with, or escalated, before they happen.

whyNot.0: Recording actual costs looks backward; forecasting looks ahead.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are set by management levels, not by forecasts.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports still provide work package status.

explain.body: Team manager to project manager; project manager to board; board to business layer.

test.q: Who decides on a forecast breach of stage tolerance?
options: The project manager
The team manager
The business layer
The project board
test.why: The project board sets stage tolerances and decides on exceptions raised against them.

whyNot.0: The project manager raises the exception report but cannot decide beyond stage tolerance.
whyNot.1: The team manager works within work package tolerance.
whyNot.2: The business layer decides on project tolerance breaches.

explain.body: If the project manager can resolve an issue within stage tolerance, no exception report is needed.

test.q: A project manager can solve a supplier delay by reordering work, and the stage stays within tolerance. What is needed?
options: An exception report
An exception plan
No exception report
A premature closure
test.why: An issue resolved within stage tolerance needs no exception report; the PM handles it in controlling a stage.

whyNot.0: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance.
whyNot.1: Exception plans follow an exception report, which is not needed here.
whyNot.3: Premature closure is a board decision for a project that should not continue.

explain.body: Escalate as soon as a breach can be forecast, so the next level has time and options.

test.q: Why should a forecast breach be escalated straight away?
options: To give the next level time and options
To let the team manager set new tolerances
To close the stage before the breach occurs
To avoid recording the issue in the register
test.why: Alerting the next level as early as possible gives it the time and options to decide what to do.

whyNot.1: Team managers do not set stage tolerances.
whyNot.2: Early escalation lets the board decide; it does not close the stage automatically.
whyNot.3: Issues are still recorded; escalation does not replace recording.
